item.title: Electronic Arts to Cut 400 Jobs, Shut Down BioWare
item.description: The next ‘Mass Effect’ will be canceled as part of the layoffs
item.dc:creator: Jason Schreier

item.title: AI Research Startup Flapping Airplanes Valued at $6 Billion in Round
item.description: Flapping Airplanes, a year-old artificial intelligence startup, has raised $1 billion in funding at a $6 billion valuation — the latest example of investors betting on a newer crop of AI research labs that have yet to introduce commercial products. The financing, set to be announced Wednesday, was led by Index Ventures and Lux Capital. Other participants included Sequoia Capital, Alphabet Inc.’s GV and Kleiner Perkins. The company’s valuation, which includes the money raised, has quadrupled fro
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz

item.title: Musk Weighs Massive SpaceX Tesla Merger
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Wall Street splits on AI as Ken Griffin warns of a bubble and Larry Fink says keep building. Musk weighs a $3.5 trillion SpaceX-Tesla tie-up. United warns on rising fuel costs, while Netflix growth slows. Plus, Per Franzen on AI overinvestment, Matthew Condon on Netflix’s next act, and Sagar Gupta joins us on activist opportunities in tech and media. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SpaceX, Tesla Boards Study Possible $3.5 Trillion Merger
item.description: Elon Musk openly endorsed the prospect of combining SpaceX with Tesla Inc. in what would be the biggest-ever corporate merger, uniting assets from electric cars to AI data centers to rocket and satellite capabilities. Bloomberg's Sana Pashankar joined Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss this as well as SpaceX's recent earnings. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apollo Fund Touts NY Yankees Financing as ‘AI-Resilient Leisure’
item.description: To understand just how much private-credit managers want to distance themselves from software loans, consider this description of the New York Yankees: “AI-resilient leisure.”
item.dc:creator: Olivia Fishlow

item.title: Nasdaq 100 Climbs as SpaceX Results Fuel AI Trade
item.description: A blockbuster earnings report from SpaceX spurred a rally in technology stocks, easing concerns over whether a global investment spree in artificial intelligence can prove sustainable. Aaron Kennon, Co-Founder & CEO at Clear Harbor Asset Management discusses the markets and the AI trade. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stord Acquires AMS Fulfillment in Nine-Figure Deal
item.description: E-Commerce logistics provider Stord made its largest acquisition to date acquiring competitor AMS Fulfillment. The deal includes 10 warehouses, which will bring Stord's global network to over 100 locations. Sean Henry, CEO and founder of Stord discusses the deal as well as the overall outlook for the shipping and logistics space. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inflation Pressures Tell us There is Speed Limit to AI Buildout, Says Coronado
item.description: A wild card for US interest rates is the trajectory of the artificial-intelligence investment boom and its impact on stock market valuation. Julia Coronado, President and Founder of MacroPolicy Perspectives, discusses the US economy, wage growth, and the impact of AI on the inflation picture. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AT&T Falls on Earnings Miss; Netflix Reports Slowing Growth | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Super Micro Computer (SMCI) jumped after reporting preliminary quarterly results that topped analysts’ estimates. The server maker said sales will be $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion in the quarter that ended Sept. 30. Analysts, on average, estimated $15 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Gross margins will be in the range of 12% to 12.5%, Super Micro said Tuesday in a statement. - AT&T (T) shares fall after it reported third-quarter wireless postpaid phone net additions that missed the average analyst estimate. - Netflix (NFLX) reported its slowest sales jump in three years and forecast a fourth consecutive quarter of slowing growth, a projection that amplifies concerns about the performance of the world’s leading online TV network. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Screentime 2027 Highlights
item.description: Bloomberg Screentime gathers the moguls, celebrities and entrepreneurs shaping the future of pop culture. In 2026, against a backdrop of rapid industry consolidation, top entertainment leaders and Bloomberg journalists converged in Los Angeles to debate what’s next for studios, live sports, podcasting, creator economies, music and the impact of AI on the creative industries. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Intel Touts Factory Expansion Progress in Sign of Growing Demand
item.description: Intel Corp. touted progress with its long-delayed US factory expansion, saying it was finishing up a plant in Arizona and making headway on the chipmaker’s newest site in Ohio.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: SpaceX, Tesla Boards Study Possible $3.5 Trillion Merger
item.description: Elon Musk openly endorsed the prospect of combining SpaceX with Tesla in what would be the biggest-ever corporate merger. Ed Ludlow has more on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Blackstone Nears Deal to Lease London Office to Fast-Growing Fintech Stripe
item.description: Stripe LLC is close to signing a lease to take space at a London office owned by Blackstone Inc, as the company seeks to accommodate its rapid expansion.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Voase

item.title: Anson Funds Bets on AI Activism
item.description: Anson Funds is preparing to launch an activist fund targeting small and mid-cap tech, media, and telecom companies. Portfolio manager Sagar Gupta joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why he sees AI as a catalyst for growth. He also discusses Lionsgate's valuable content library and potential strategic interest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: EBay to Ax 9% of Staff in Second Round of Job Cuts in 2026
item.description: EBay Inc. will eliminate 9% of its workforce, according to a person familiar with the matter, marking the company’s second round of job cuts this year.
item.dc:creator: Spencer Soper

item.title: US Urges Fix for Widely Used Software After Critical Alerts
item.description: The US government is working to address and stop any potential cybersecurity issues stemming from flaws in PHP, a widely used open-source software, that may impact federal agencies and American critical infrastructure, according to a White House official.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gallagher and Patrick Van Oosterom

item.title: AT&T Boosts Profit Outlook But SpaceX Threat Weighs on Stock
item.description: AT&T Inc. showed strong gains in internet and mobile phone customers in the third quarter, but it wasn’t enough to assuage market concerns about the looming entry of SpaceX into the consumer cellular market.
item.dc:creator: Kelcee Griffis

item.title: Meta Earnings Will Provide a Gut Check for Struggling AI Trade
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc.’s earnings arrive as investors grow anxious about the state of the artificial intelligence trade, offering a chance to calm a few nerves — or exacerbate those fears.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Vlastelica

item.title: AI Fears Return With Neocloud Elice’s 32% Debut Flop
item.description: Shares of data-center infrastructure company Elice Inc. plunged in their trading debut, underscoring lingering concerns about whether the artificial intelligence boom can justify the billions of dollars being poured into the industry.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee and Youkyung Lee

item.title: Korea Data Center IPO to Test AI Investor Resolve
item.description: Data-center infrastructure company Elice Inc. is poised to debut on South Korea’s tech-heavy Kosdaq market Tuesday, testing AI investors’ nerves after peer Firmus canceled its high-profile listing this month.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee
